heading: Large batches can hurt generalization under fixed epoch budgets
definition: with the number of epochs held fixed, image classifiers and language models trained with batches beyond a workload-dependent size reach worse held-out performance than with smaller batches (Keskar et al. 2017; Shallue et al. 2019). Longer training, learning-rate scaling with warmup, and normalization or regularization changes can shrink or remove the penalty, and some image classifiers match small-batch accuracy within the same epoch budget (Hoffer et al. 2017; Goyal et al. 2017).
summary: Several independent groups reproduce a large-batch penalty in image classifiers and language models under fixed epoch or token budgets. Longer training can reduce the penalty, and adapted training recipes sometimes remove it within the same epoch budget.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 at <1B and 1–10B; R1 at 10–100B for one-epoch LoRA downstream accuracy, based on a supplied header marking shared authorship with an original; fixed-epoch pretraining-loss replication remains unresolved. Toy and >100B: ?; counts: versions.V5.studies_by_size has neither category.
suggested_status.reason: Independent records support the conditional batch-penalty and recovery pattern. ImageNet LARS recipes approximately preserve AlexNet and ResNet-50 accuracy within common epoch budgets (10.1145/3225058.3225069#R2, 10.1145/3225058.3225069#R3, 10.1145/3225058.3225069#R11, 10.1145/3225058.3225069#R16). Matched-token 160M nanoGPT comparisons show deterioration with momentum SGD but substantially greater batch tolerance with tuned Adam (arXiv:2506.12543#R1, arXiv:2506.12543#R2, arXiv:2506.12543#R3). Repeated-data 1.5B decoder training reports worse validation cross-entropy with larger batches at matched epochs (arXiv:2610.15965#R4). One-epoch MetaMathQA LoRA experiments report fixed-sample degradation beyond an optimal batch range, with consistent trends across LLaMA-2-7B and 13B models (arXiv:2602.09492#R1, arXiv:2602.09492#R4). The LARS, nanoGPT and repeated-data decoder headers do not mark shared authorship with an original. The supplied header for arXiv:2602.09492 marks shared authorship with an original, so its evidence counts as R1 rather than independent replication under the synthesis rules; actual author overlap is not established by the paper text. Counts: versions.V5.verdicts.supports.studies = 221, versions.V5.verdicts.limits_scope.studies = 110, and versions.V5.verdicts.challenges.studies = 6; these are overlapping categories, not votes establishing universality.
suggested_status.open_questions: Matched-protocol independent tests showing that established penalties disappear after adequate tuning would strengthen a C interpretation for those conditions. Independent one-epoch LoRA replication at 10–100B would strengthen that scale's R1 assessment to R2. Fixed-epoch pretraining-loss tests at 10–100B and explicitly identified >100B models would clarify scale coverage. Isolated language-model warmup and normalization interventions would clarify which recovery components transfer across workloads.

source.title: On Large-Batch Training for Deep Learning: Generalization Gap and Sharp Minima
source.authors: N. Keskar; Dheevatsa Mudigere; J. Nocedal; M. Smelyanskiy; P. Tang

original_result.setup: Keskar et al. swept batch size for C1 on CIFAR-10 using ADAM for 100 epochs.
original_result.result: Test accuracy declines beyond a batch size of approximately 500. Separate accuracy comparisons stopped training based on loss, so they do not establish the effect of batch size under a fixed epoch budget.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

untested.what: Batch penalties and recovery interventions in models explicitly stated to exceed 100B parameters.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V5.studies_by_size has no >100B entry. The supplied partials and packs provide no explicitly identified test above that scale. The substantial 'not stated' size category prevents concluding that every underlying model is smaller.

untested.what: Separate causal contributions of warmup and normalization changes to recovery of an established language-model batch penalty, with the remaining recipe and training exposure controlled.
untested.basis: The cited studies' untested-parts lines leave these isolated interventions unresolved. Successful combined scaling/warmup recipes, regularization interventions and adaptive schedules elsewhere prevent treating language-model recovery generally as untested. counts: versions.V5.coverage_by_operation, versions.V5.studies_by_family and versions.V5.studies_by_stage establish broader coverage but do not identify these component ablations.

untested.what: The critical constant batch size for the customer-task SFT workloads and the LLaMA batch-ramping workloads.
untested.basis: arXiv:2609.01244's untested-parts line leaves the critical threshold and batches beyond its tested range unresolved. For arXiv:2609.39767, Figure 5's constant-batch sweep holds iterations fixed, Figure 6's fixed-token comparison varies ramp timing, and Section 5 schedules batches without estimating critical batch size. A constant-batch, equal-token threshold remains unestablished; this is an inferred coverage gap, not an explicit untested-parts statement by the paper. Figure 7's lower validation loss with late batch increases supports V5's recipe-adaptation exception but does not establish that threshold. No other partial supplies those workload-specific sweeps. counts: versions.V5.studies_by_stage and versions.V5.coverage_by_operation.scaling show stage and scaling coverage, without establishing these thresholds.

wording_issues.issue: Adaptation is not sufficient for recovery at every horizon. Linear scaling with warmup can diverge. In incomplete TinyLlama/C4 pretraining at matched sequence budgets, adaptive schedules yield validation losses 5.671, 5.704 and 5.113, worse than fixed-8192's 4.893 and fixed-4096's 3.817: adaptation increases the penalty. Seesaw retains deficits in some settings. In DIVEBATCH's CIFAR-10 comparisons without learning-rate rescaling, fixed SGD batch 2048 leads batch 128 by 1.85 and 2.23 percentage points at the 25% and 50% checkpoints, against small-batch baselines 85.13±0.36% and 88.88±0.56%; at the final budget it trails by 3.03 percentage points against 95.50±0.02%. The body's conditional recovery wording accommodates incomplete recovery; the title needs the same qualification and an explicit horizon.

wording_issues.phrase: with the number of epochs held fixed
wording_issues.issue: Distinguish equal epochs, matched token/example exposure, fixed updates, loss-target stopping and equal execution time. Keskar's main accuracy comparisons train without budget limits until loss stops improving, so they cannot determine the fixed-epoch effect; Figure 4 separately tests a fixed-epoch sweep. The Hessian study uses loss-target stopping and does not establish fixed epochs; its moderate-batch improvements and scaling experiment add no scope restriction to V5. In CIFAR-5m, larger batches perform worse at matched samples seen in both online and offline training; equal-step online comparisons favor larger batches. Matched exposure on the fixed offline subset also establishes equal epochs. Scion uses a matched token budget. These protocols should retain their budget labels.

The measured boundary also depends on optimizer, recipe and training horizon. MuLoCo retains performance over ranges where comparator optimizers deteriorate. For 160M nanoGPT at matched 1.3B-token exposure, validation perplexities at batches 64/256/1024 are 30.76/33.08/65.94 with momentum SGD and 28.77/28.20/29.36 with Adam: SGD worsens across batches, whereas Adam improves at 256 and remains comparatively similar at 1024. Within-batch optimizer rankings alone do not test V5. Private-training responses depend on optimizer and dataset. TinyCNN favors an intermediate batch under its fixed training budget. Stable or improving finite ranges do not establish a harmful threshold outside the measured range.

Specify the batch definition. Batch augmentation repeats transformed instances while preserving distinct-example and update counts. Local SGD processes 16384 samples per synchronization with K=16, H=8 and local batch 128, reaching 92.0%; ordinary SGD reaches 92.5% at batch 2048 and 76.3% at 16384. Accumulated micro-batches can change normalization statistics: on CIFAR-100, micro-batch 10 accumulates to effective batch 128 and reaches 62.97±0.30%, versus 59.08±0.31% at batch 512; the latter is not established as effective batch 128. Adaptive ImageNet batches 4096–16384 match fixed 4096 over 90 epochs, but also use a different learning-rate multiplier. These interventions do not isolate constant batches containing more distinct examples.

Name the endpoint metric. For single-GPU CIFAR-100 ResNet-18 at 95 epochs, increasing batches from 32 to 64–256 worsens accuracy while improving test loss. CIFAR-10 ResNet-56 equal-time recipes improve accuracy while worsening validation loss, with learning rates and epochs also changed. Nano-V3 Muon at a fixed 3T-token horizon has coding scores 62.23/63.70/61.89 and math scores 82.52/81.57/81.47 at 1x/2x/3x batches, showing endpoint-dependent orderings. In shallow Romanian-English translation with delayed updates, warmup leaves a smaller BLEU penalty and numerically better validation cross-entropy. That partial recovery supports V5's adaptation clause; it is not an additional scope restriction.

Keep held-out outcomes distinct from a training–test gap and from training-loss proxies. The Muon/Gemma study uses fresh-batch training loss without a separate held-out dataset. Extreme ImageNet penalties include optimization failure. The frequency study's testing-accuracy ordering differs from its generalization-gap ordering; other comparisons show both training and test losses worsening.

Distinguish approximate agreement, published benchmarks, matched within-optimizer controls and target attainment. LAMB retains published BERT and ImageNet benchmarks while larger-batch results remain below its own small-batch controls. These residual penalties support V5's conditional recovery claim; they limit an unqualified claim of complete recovery. The ImageNet sweep supplies no statistical significance assessment. The mixed-precision study uses published references. FOP establishes reaching a common target; MERIT preserves a downstream task average while changing optimizer. Small numerical differences without adequate uncertainty do not establish exact equality or statistical equivalence.

SWAP's recovery matches epochs per trajectory while using parallel small-batch refinement and averaging. It does not establish equal aggregate training work or recovery while keeping batches large throughout.

Retain task and training-stage labels. LAMB varies BERT pretraining batches but evaluates SQuAD after fixed downstream fine-tuning; its residual within-LAMB penalties support V5. ScaLA evaluates GLUE adaptation. The XLNet example measures Yelp sentiment classification; its tested batches do not establish a harmful threshold, so it supplies task coverage rather than a V5 scope limit. GRPO/PPO comparisons use retained-response budgets. In GRPO, P=128 is the learning-rate reference; the descriptive alignment band surrounds a mean fitted from P=64–1024. Penalties at P=2048–4096 with scaling alone support V5 rather than limit it. These downstream and RL outcomes do not directly measure held-out language-model pretraining loss.

Keep this remedy conditional and distinguish duration from accompanying schedule changes. Extreme/full-batch image classifiers can retain deficits after extended training. The mLSTM intervention changes duration and decay together; low-resource NMT retains significant deficits after extension. Granite instruction tuning shows benchmark-specific batch-ranking crossovers rather than a universal longer-training remedy.

method_sensitivity.factor: Budget axis, training horizon and stopping rule
method_sensitivity.what: Shallue reports larger-batch advantages under update budgets and smaller-batch advantages under constrained epoch budgets. ResNet-18/CIFAR-5m comparisons favor larger batches at equal updates but smaller batches at matched samples, for batches 32, 128 and 512; matched samples imply matched epochs only for the fixed offline subset. DIVEBATCH's unadapted batch-2048 ResNet-20 exceeds batch-128 SGD at early matched checkpoints on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 but trails at the final budget; the early advantages occur at 25% and 50% on CIFAR-10 and 25% on CIFAR-100. Repeated-data decoder comparisons include matched-epoch tests and independently optimized stopping epochs; batch 64 also beats batch 16 later in training. Fixed iterations, equal time, loss-target stopping and epoch caps describe different comparisons.

At matched token budgets, nanoGPT perplexities at batches 64/256/1024 are 30.76/33.08/65.94 for momentum SGD and 28.77/28.20/29.36 for Adam. Over 90 epochs, ResNet34/ImageNet accuracy at batches 256→4096 falls for SGD (70.64→49.35%), Adam (65.06→54.96%) and AdamW (69.64→68.40%), but rises for Lamb (69.17→70.34%) and ALTO (69.95→70.83%). AdaBelief changes from 70.12% to 70.18%, without uncertainty establishing a meaningful difference. Scratch ResNet50/CIFAR-10 with RAdam learning rate 0.01 improves learned-feature SVM accuracy from 57.3% at batch 32 to 72.2% at 256 after 50 epochs; other learning rates reverse the trend. Scaling Adam's second-moment decay to preserve token half-life converts a 19M C4 model's small-batch disadvantage into parity at 705M tokens.

method_sensitivity.factor: Learning-rate scaling, warmup shape and usable batch range
method_sensitivity.what: Goyal's batch-8k ResNet-50 validation errors are 24.84±0.37% without warmup, 25.88±0.56% with constant warmup and 23.74±0.09% with gradual warmup over 90 epochs. On CIFAR-10 ResNet34, linear scaling with warmup helps intermediate batches but worsens results or diverges at larger batches over 200 epochs. LEGW combines square-root scaling and extended warmup to preserve PTB-small performance through batch 640 over 13 epochs. Adaptive-SDE experiments obtain language-model trajectory agreement with square-root Adam scaling, but incomplete RoBERTa training and wall-clock caps limit endpoint comparisons.

Ghost-batch-normalized ImageNet ResNet50-V2 nearly preserves accuracy from batch 256 to 4096 over 90 epochs, while Fixup and SkipInit deteriorate; matched cross-batch comparisons show dropout shrinks their penalties. Separately, adapted ResNet-50 training over 100 epochs leaves batch-8192 versus batch-256 penalties of 0.30 percentage points with EMA evaluation and 0.19 with PreciseBN. MegDet at optimization batch 64 reaches 35.3 mmAP with BN size 64 versus 37.1 with BN sizes 16 or 32. Over 150 epochs, CIFAR-100 KNResNet-50 accuracy changes from 80.18±0.10% at batch 32 to 80.09±0.26% at 256. These uncertainties are run standard deviations; no significance or equivalence test establishes absence of a penalty. Very-small-batch BatchNorm failure does not test V5's above-threshold prediction.

method_sensitivity.factor: Regularizer, noise structure and optimizer interaction
method_sensitivity.what: For ResNet32/CIFAR-100 SGD, batch-128→2000 accuracy changes from 73.61% to 65.38% without weight decay and 77.73% to 76.87% with it. Fisher-trace and gradient-norm recovery depends on regularization micro-batch size; Tiny-ImageNet uses sample penalties. Jacobian penalties fail under the reported update-based or training-accuracy stopping budgets, which do not establish equal-epoch recovery. At equal updates, combined label flipping and output-gradient noise recovers CIFAR-100 VGG19 small-batch accuracy. Initially, σ_ln × sqrt(E[||z||₂²]) = 0.1 and label-flipping probability is 0.1; both halve at each learning-rate annealing. Spherical Gaussian parameter noise leaves a substantial deficit; its plotted σ values are standard deviations. LAWN approximately preserves Adam performance but leaves larger residual penalties with SGD or LAMB in specified comparisons.

method_sensitivity.factor: Batch construction and timing of batch increases
method_sensitivity.what: Batch augmentation enlarges effective batches through transformed repetitions while retaining distinct-example counts and update schedules; PTB repetitions use different dropout masks. Mix & Match changes image resolution, batch size and additional recipe components together. ImageNet ResNet-50 reaches 76.1% with fixed batch 8192 for 90 epochs on half a TPU pod, and with batch 8192 for 30 epochs followed by 16384 for 60 epochs using the full pod. Keeping batch 16384 throughout with doubled initial learning rate loses accuracy. LLaMA experiments at equal total tokens report worse final validation performance after early batch increases and lower validation loss after late increases with a warmup-stable learning rate. These verdict-only timing findings support V5's recipe-adaptation qualification.

method_sensitivity.factor: Local updates, synchronization, workers and communication
method_sensitivity.what: At H=32 and 200 epochs, ImageNet ResNet-101 adaptive local-training schedules reach 50.61% or 49.13%, above fixed batch 13000's 38.77% but below batch 6000's 59.20%. CIFAR-10 ResNet-20 MB-SGD and PL-SGD both deteriorate as local batch increases from 128 to 1024 over 300 epochs. Hierarchical Crossover-SGD's sharp effective-batch drop with four groups is absent with eight groups. In near-IID federated CIFAR-10 training with two local epochs and 200 rounds, ResNet-18 accuracy fractions are 0.680, corrected 0.534 and 0.383 at batch 32, batch 128 and full batch.

method_sensitivity.factor: Data distribution, selection, objective and training stage
method_sensitivity.what: In arXiv:2312.02517, highly class-imbalanced CIFAR favors smaller batches under the stated default training budget; nearly flat balanced-data curves do not establish that the workload-dependent threshold was exceeded. Separately, TDDS-selected CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 coresets with ResNet-18 favor smaller batches at 80% and 90% pruning over 200 epochs: the comparisons are batch 128 versus 64 and batch 128 versus 32, respectively. TDDS tests pruning rather than class imbalance and does not directly measure its proposed overfitting mechanism. SSA-CLR generally benefits from larger batches over 64–512, which also changes the contrastive negative pool. Granite 7B instruction tuning initially favors batch 3840 over 7680 at matched samples, but the larger batch overtakes after approximately 3.75 million samples on MMLU and 8.5 million on MTBench. Granite and the imbalance sweep lack extracted comparison rows.

method_sensitivity.factor: Privacy noise, tuning scope and adversarial aggregation
method_sensitivity.what: Over ten ImageNet fine-tuning epochs, private full-model LAMB accuracy rises from 68.2% to 71.1% for ViT-B/16 and 55.6% to 70.1% for ResNet50x4 as batches increase from 2^17 to 2^20; noise is recalibrated to preserve privacy. Non-private ViT-B/16 LAMB falls from 81.7% to 73.1%. Private last-layer Momentum ViT-B/16 rises from 61.3% to 65.3% at those endpoints, below 66.6% at 2^19; ResNet50x4 rises from 39.6% to 49.2%. WRN-16-4/CIFAR-10 DP-SGD at ε=4 is described as flat over batches 256–4096, at 37.0–39.7%; CIFAR-100 instead peaks and declines, and spectral DP-Muon improves over much of the tested range. ByzSGDm declines without attacks (δ=0), improves under KR/ALIE, and remains at 10.00% under complete KR/FoE failure.

ResNet-18/CIFAR-100 intermediate batch increases lower test loss while reducing classification accuracy; loss is 1.823 at batch 32 and 1.748 at 256 over 95 epochs. Nano-V3 Muon coding improves from 62.23 to 63.70 at 2× batch while math falls from 82.52 to 81.57 at a fixed 3T-token horizon. Centralized CIFAR-10 PGD training with vanilla SGD over 350 epochs and ℓ∞ 8/255 attacks improves final AA accuracy from 33.84% to 35.86% at global batches 1024 versus 2048 while final clean accuracy falls from 78.68% to 71.44%; this comparison is verdict-only. Best checkpoints are selected by PGD robust validation accuracy. Shallow Romanian-English NMT warmup gives lower BLEU but better validation cross-entropy; this adaptation fits V5's recovery qualification.
